tldr: Headlines across all 12 regions converge on a single frame: an escalating US-Iran air war over the Strait of Hormuz, with most outlets anchoring coverage to the consecutive-night strike count; Iran International alone foregrounds growing talk of a ground assault, while outlets from the US, Turkey, and India separately elevate Trump's tit-for-tat infrastructure ultimatum as the political headline, and Egypt and Pan-African coverage surface the oil-embargo and tanker-blockade dimension absent from most other titles.
event_summary: The US military has now conducted 13 consecutive nights of strikes on Iran targeting military infrastructure across the country, while Tehran has blockaded the Strait of Hormuz and stopped oil tankers; President Trump publicly threatened to destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every Iranian attack on commercial shipping in the strait.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet to frame the US military campaign as strategically evolving rather than repeating: 'ground assault talk grows' and 'moving deeper into southern Iran' position the strikes as systematic degradation building toward possible land operations — a narrative absent from every other headline in the corpus.

'Not a single drop of oil' is the most categorical economic-threat headline in the corpus — the sole title to foreground Iran's counter-escalation as a global energy embargo rather than a military retaliation, framing the Strait closure as an existential supply-chain event.

'Will reimpose blockade' is the only headline to name a US blockade against Iran as a distinct instrument of coercion alongside the air strikes, foregrounding the economic-siege dimension that body texts discuss but which almost no other outlet surfaced at the title layer.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the story is almost entirely a consecutive-night military strike counter — every outlet anchors to the strike cadence and Hormuz standoff — with Trump's infrastructure ultimatum as the secondary hook and the oil-embargo and potential ground-assault dimensions visible only in isolated outlier titles.
